facts.fact_text: The applicant attempted to participate in a demonstration organised by the opposition on 20 October 2012.
Despite the Baku City Executive Authority's refusal to authorise the demonstration at the originally indicated place, the organisers decided to hold the demonstration as planned.
According to the applicant, the demonstration of 20 October 2012 was intended to be peaceful.
According to the applicant, the demonstration of 20 October 2012 was conducted in a peaceful manner.
The participants in the demonstration of 20 October 2012 were demanding democratic reforms in the country.
On 6 May 2014 the applicant participated in an assembly that took place near the Baku Court of Serious Crimes.
The protest outside the Baku Court of Serious Crimes on 6 May 2014 was brief, spontaneous and peaceful.
As soon as the protesters outside the Baku Court of Serious Crimes on 6 May 2014 started chanting slogans, police officers and people in plain clothes began to forcibly disperse the assembly.
The Baku City Executive Authority (BCEA) refused to authorise the holding of the demonstration at the place indicated by the organisers.
Shortly after the applicant's attempt to march to the assembly on 20 October 2012, he was arrested and taken to a police station.
As soon as the protesters outside the Baku Court of Serious Crimes on 6 May 2014 started chanting slogans, police officers and people in plain clothes began to forcibly disperse the assembly.

At the time of both of the applicant's arrests (20 October 2012 and 6 May 2014), under Article 5 § IV of the Law on Freedom of Assembly of 13 November 1998, no prior written notification was required for spontaneous assemblies.

At the time of the applicant's arrest on 20 October 2012, Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 (CAO) provided that any breach of the rules, set forth under the legislation, on the organisation and holding of assemblies, demonstrations, protests, marches and pickets shall be punishable by a reprimand or a fine of seven to thirteen manats (AZN).

At the time of the applicant's arrest on 20 October 2012, Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences of 2000 (CAO) provided that deliberate failure by an individual to comply with a lawful order of a police officer or military serviceman carrying out their duties to protect public order shall be punishable by a fine of twenty to twenty-five manats (AZN) or, if that sanction is inadequate in the circumstances of the case and taking into account the character of the offender, by administrative detention for a term of up to fifteen days.

Under the amendment introduced by Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012, participation in an assembly organised in breach of the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies became explicitly punishable under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).

Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 introduced for the first time a punishment in the form of administrative detention of up to fifteen days under Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).
Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 introduced community service as a new form of punishment under Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO).

Law no. 462-IVQD of 2 November 2012 increased the fine for breaching the rules on the organisation and holding of assemblies, fixing the amounts as follows: between AZN 300 and 600 for participants of an assembly; between AZN 1,500 and 3,000 for individuals who organise an assembly; between AZN 3,000 and 6,000 for persons in charge (vəzifəli şəxslər) who organise an assembly; and between AZN 15,000 and 30,000 for legal entities involved in the organisation of an assembly.
Law no. 651-IVQD of 14 May 2013 increased the administrative-detention sentence set out in Article 298 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) to up to two months.
Law no. 457-IVQD of 2 November 2012 increased the fine in Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) to AZN 200.
Law no. 651-IVQD of 14 May 2013 increased the administrative-detention sentence in Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) to up to one month.
According to the applicant, he was never served with copies of the administrative-offence reports in his case files in either case.
According to the applicant, he was never served with other documents in his case files in either case.
In both cases (20 October 2012 and 6 May 2014), the applicant was not given access to a lawyer after his arrest or while in police custody.
In the second case (6 May 2014), according to a document drawn up by a police officer and an order dated 6 May 2014, a State-funded lawyer (Mr S.A.) was instructed to assist the applicant.
In both cases (before the Binagadi District Court on 20 October 2012 and before the Nasimi District Court on 7 May 2014), State-funded lawyers were appointed to assist the applicant.
According to the records of the court hearings in both cases, in their oral submissions the State-funded lawyers briefly stated that the applicant was not guilty.

In both cases, the only witnesses questioned during the court hearing were police officers who, according to the official records, had arrested the applicant or prepared an administrative-offence report on him.
In both cases, the first-instance court found that the applicant had failed to stop participating in an unauthorised protest.

By a decision of 20 October 2012, the Binagadi District Court convicted the applicant under Article 310.1 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) and sentenced him to ten days' administrative detention.

By a decision of 7 May 2014, the Nasimi District Court convicted the applicant under Article 298.2 of the Code of Administrative Offences (CAO) and sentenced him to fifteen days' administrative detention.
